entities.summary: William Erwin Eisner was an American cartoonist, writer, and entrepreneur. He was one of the earliest cartoonists to work in the American comic book industry, and his series The Spirit (1940–1952) was noted for its experiments in content and form. In 1978, he popularized the term "graphic novel" with the publication of his book A Contract with God. He was an early contributor to formal comics studies with his book Comics and Sequential Art (1985). The Eisner Award was named in his honor and is given to recognize achievements each year in the comics medium; he was one of the three inaugural inductees to the Will Eisner Comic Book Hall of Fame.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Will Eisner's work in comics and sequential art helped establish the medium as a legitimate form of storytelling, paving the way for future generations of cartoonists and writers. His influence can be seen in many contemporary comics and graphic novels.
